festivals: Maha Shivaratri (falls on Magha Bahula Dasami; the major festival)

history.dynasty: Kota chiefs; Vijayanagara Empire (patronized by Sri Krishnadevaraya)
history.period: 11th century CE (earliest inscription 1129 CE); renovated late 18th century
history.summary: Amareswara Swamy Temple at Amaravathi is one of the five sacred Pancharama Kshetras of Shiva, and the only one on the Krishna River (the others are in the Godavari region). Based on epigraphical evidence the temple originated in the 11th century, with the earliest of its 35 inscriptions dated 1129 CE; it was patronized by the Kota chiefs and the Vijayanagara Empire, including Sri Krishnadevaraya, and underwent major renovations in the late 18th century. Built in the Dravidian style with four gopurams on the small Krouncha Shaila hillock, it enshrines a 15-foot white marble Sivalinga, so tall that priests mount a pedestal platform for rituals. Legend says the lingam was installed by Indra (hence Amararama, 'abode of the immortals'), and that it kept growing until a nail was hammered into its top to stop it, leaving a red stain visible today.

name: Amareswara Swamy Temple
town_description: Amaravathi (Amaravati) is an ancient temple town in Palnadu district on the banks of the Krishna River, famed both as the home of the Amararama Shiva temple and as the historic Satavahana-era capital region of Andhra Pradesh with the celebrated Amaravati Buddhist stupa nearby. The village is named after the temple itself, and Andhra Pradesh's planned new capital city, Amaravati, lies about 35 km to the east.

travel.airport: Vijayawada International Airport (Gannavaram) (approx. 60 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Peddakurapadu (approx. 19 km); Guntur Junction (approx. 32 km) is the nearest major railway junction.
travel.road: About 33 km from Guntur and 42-46 km from Vijayawada by road; well connected by APSRTC buses and private taxis via the Guntur-Amaravathi highway.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Maha Shivaratri (February-March) is the most vibrant time to visit, and the Karthika month (November-December) is also special. Early mornings and evenings are best to avoid the midday heat.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 1:00 PM; evening 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM (break 1:00 PM to 4:00 PM). Daily abhishekam is performed 6:00 AM to 11:45 AM. Traditional dress is expected; photography and mobile phones are not allowed inside.
